text.p: A court sentenced a French surgeon, once branded the "scalpel samurai", to six years in jail on Monday for unnecessary operations on men suspected of suffering from prostate cancer.

The court also stripped doctor Georges Rossignol of the right to vote and other civic privileges for 10 years after finding him guilty of "deliberate violence having caused mutilations or permanent infirmity".
"I am an innocent victim of a true injustice," Rossignol said after the ruling by the court in Toulouse, southwestern France. "I never deliberately mutilated anyone."
His lawyer said he might appeal.

The court ruled that Rossignol, a urologist, had cut prostate glands from six men based on what a panel of court-appointed medical experts ruled were erroneous diagnoses of cancer. Prosecutors said he resorted too zealously to surgery to boost his income and reputation.

The court cleared a co-defendant, doctor Pierre Leandri, on similar charges concerning two patients, but ordered a new expert medical review of his treatment of a third. "I think that the court gave me back my honour," Leandri said.
Surgery aims to remove cancerous tissue from the prostate gland, which opens into the urethra at the base of the penis. But the surgery can have side-effects like incontinence and impotence.
During a trial in December, prosecutor Herve Robin called the two surgeons "scalpel samurais who committed the worst of crimes for a doctor by betraying the confidence of their patients."

Prostate cancer is common among elderly men -- former French president Francois Mitterrand died from it in 1996 after a 15-year illness. Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko underwent prostate surgery in Switzerland last year.
